payload.headline: Apple rises 1.9% to 349.08, still priced above every value estimate

summary.thesis: Apple is a strong, cash-rich business, but at 349.08 the price assumes faster cash growth than Apple is showing, while analysts keep cutting their forecasts.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait, because the price sits between nearby support and resistance with little room to gain.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy at or below 300.56; swing entry on a close above 351.46 or a hold of 342.73–345.08

payload.happening: Apple closed at 349.08, up 1.9% on the day, and is moving sideways (trend: range) around its flat 20-day average of 347.58. Since the last note, the news has been minor. A startup reportedly sued Apple in India over a contact-sharing feature, and AirPods Pro 3 are reportedly 40 percent off ahead of Black Friday. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-28.
payload.business: Some facts change the business itself. Sales over the last twelve months were 478.8B, up from 416.2B. Free cash flow (the cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. The operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) improved to 33.01% from 31.97%. Those are real strengths. The concern is momentum and stock on hand. Year-over-year sales growth in the latest quarter slowed to 11.72%, down from 16.6% two quarters earlier. Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%. Unsold products can force price cuts, which would hurt margins. The 40 percent AirPods discount is reported, not confirmed by a filing, and is one small data point in that direction. Analysts cut next-quarter earnings-per-share forecasts by 3.8% over 30 days. Other facts mainly affect sentiment or governance: the reported India lawsuit, a new investigation risk in the annual report, and the reported Ted Lasso renewal. None of these changes demand or cash today. At risk is how fast earnings grow. Not at risk is Apple's ability to produce cash. Net debt of 23.4B (debt above cash) is small next to 136.1B of yearly free cash flow.

worth.text: At 349.08, Apple trades at 38.9 times trailing earnings and 32.9 times next year's forecast earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio (market value divided by yearly sales) is 10.6. That compares with a peer median of 4.8 and sits at the 97th percentile of Apple's own last five years. A discounted cash flow model (which adds up future cash and converts it to today's dollars) gives 143.11 in the bear case, 198.72 in the base case and 260.24 in the bull case. If Apple returned to its usual price-to-sales range, the stock would be worth 222.1–300.56. To justify today's price, free cash flow would need to start growing at about 26.9% a year. Last year's sales grew 15%, and sales grew about 8% a year over three years. Starting growth is what drives the gap: at 20% the value is 268.08, and at 30% it is 392.11. My range runs from the DCF bear case to the top of Apple's own history.
worth.key_assumption: How fast free cash flow grows at the start: the price needs about 26.9% a year, while sales grew 15% last year and about 7.7% a year over three years.

bull: Free cash flow jumped to 136.1B from 98.8B a year earlier, a 28.41% free-cash-flow margin.
The operating margin rose to 33.01% from 31.97%, so profit is growing faster than sales.
The share count fell 1.56% in a year, so each remaining share owns more of the business.
bear: The price of 349.08 is above the top of every value method, which tops out at 300.56.
Inventory is up 154% against 12% sales growth, which can lead to discounts and lower margins.
Analysts cut next-quarter earnings forecasts by 3.8% over 30 days, and next-year forecasts by 2.3%.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above the whole value range of 143.11–300.56, so it is too high to buy.
The top of my range and of Apple's own price-to-sales history, close to the rising 200-day average of 303.15. Buying starts here.
The value if free cash flow starts growing at 20%, still faster than last year's 15% sales growth. Adding makes sense here.

longterm.why: The business is high quality, but the price needs growth Apple is not showing, and forecasts are falling. The rule verdict is 'Too expensive' and the committee call is Hold.

swing.why: The price sits inside the 347.89–351.46 zone. Support is just below at 342.73–345.08 and resistance just above at 354.07–356.15. The typical daily move (ATR, average true range) is 8.31, so there is not enough room to the upside to justify the risk, and the macro read is negative. Enter only on a close above 351.46, aiming for 359.79, or on a pullback that holds 342.73–345.08.

decision.timing: Options price a 6.8% move by 2026-12-18 and an 11.9% move by 2027-02-19, a window that includes the 2027-01-28 report. There is no long-term buy above 300.56 before that report shows whether the inventory build hurt margins.

change_mind: The price falls to 300.56 or below, the top of the value range: then buy.
The 2027-01-28 report beats the 2.91 EPS consensus and quarterly sales growth climbs back above 16.6%, which would support growth closer to what the price implies.
The operating margin falls toward 24%, which would cut the value to 200.66 and lower my buy levels.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The price rose to 349.08 but remains above the 300.56 top of the value range, and next-quarter EPS forecasts fell 3.8% in 30 days.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
